source_grounding.call_chain_traced: SearchRequest.groupParams.strictGroupSize → rankParams.strictGroupSize → QueryInfo.strict_group_size_ → CompositeGroupByMap(strict_group_size=true) → IsGroupResEnough() condition check
source_grounding.note: Source code reveals the bug: In strict mode, IsGroupResEnough() checks if enough groups reached group_size_ limit, but the iteration loop (line 219 in SearchGroupByOperator.cpp: while (iterator->HasNext() && !groupMap.IsGroupResEnough())) continues adding elements to groups even after they exceed group_size_. The Push() method rejects elements at group_size_ threshold, but this happens AFTER the element is already counted. This allows groups to accumulate group_size_+1 elements before the stopping condition triggers.

cognition_match.note: Does not match documented by_design_patterns. This appears to be a genuine implementation bug in the grouping logic, not a deliberate design choice. The strict_group_size parameter is clearly intended to enforce per-group limits but the implementation has a logic flaw.

verdicts.rationale: Source code grounding reveals a clear implementation bug in CompositeGroupByMap::Push() and IsGroupResEnough() logic. When strict_group_size=true, the code allows groups to exceed group_size_ limit because the stopping condition checks aggregate group state rather than per-group limits. The iteration continues adding elements to groups even after they hit the size threshold, resulting in groups with group_size_+1 elements. Raw evidence confirms this: with groupSize=2, all 5 groups returned 3 elements each. This is a Type1_IllegalSuccess - API accepts grouping parameters but fails to enforce the strict size constraint.
